deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 77r is a printed leaf from Thomas Babington Macaulay's *The History of England from the Accession of James II*, Chapter III ('State of England in 1685'), page 293. The typography and the running heads ('STATE OF ENGLAND IN 1685.' on the recto, 'HISTORY OF ENGLAND.' on p. 294) suggest a mid-nineteenth-century edition, possibly an American reprint, but that is only a guess. Volumes I–II first appeared in December 1848, which fits the footnote on the next page about 'the troubles which have lately agitated Paris'.

The text runs as follows:
- It ends a paragraph on English regiments kept in foreign (Dutch) service, followed by a footnote on Macaulay's sources for the army: the Historical Records of Regiments, Chamberlayne's State of England (1684), the Abridgment of the English Military Discipline (1685) and the Exercise of Foot (1690).
- It then begins the section marked 'The navy.' This argues that Parliament distrusted a standing army but readily funded the fleet. It contrasts Naseby and Dunbar with the Armada and Blake's victories, and cites the grant of nearly £600,000 under Danby for thirty new men of war.

The only handwriting is an archival pencil foliation '77' in the right margin, apparently struck through or underlined. The previous page carries German floor-plan sketches (Stube, Kammer, Küche, Tür, Tisch, Ofen, Bett), and the next page is Macaulay p. 294. So this leaf was evidently kept in the Varia bundle as loose or scrap paper. There is no derivation to reconstruct, and nothing is computed.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed page of Macaulay's History of England with no mathematical content and no annotation by Riemann. At most it shows that a leaf of a popular 1848+ history ended up among his papers, which is of no mathematical or historiographical significance.
transcription_corrections: The page is a printed book page (Macaulay, History of England, ch. III, p. 293), not a manuscript; the transcription of the printed text is essentially accurate.
The marginal 'The navy.' is a printed side-note placed beside the line beginning 'If the jealousy of the Parliament…', not a separate heading line.
The '77 [?]' is a handwritten pencil archival folio number in the right margin, apparently struck through or underlined; it is not part of the printed text.
